chunk_findings.detail: The decision document records the MUST strength mapping as `MUST (block; override = waive only)`, but the accepted operator decision in the intent is `MUST (block, waive|none)`. This omits the `none` override, so an implementation following this source-of-truth document would incorrectly make every MUST waivable and lose the ability to declare an unwaivable org floor requirement.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/decisions/requirements.md:10

chunk_findings.detail: The soft/hard rule contradicts itself: line 15 says an upgrade is SOFT when the client honours `list_changed` or facade mode is on, but line 21 makes “the shim or protocol itself changed” HARD with no exception for those cases, and line 20 says a changed schema is soft only if the worker accepts the previous arguments for one version, even for a client that honours `list_changed`. Given a client that honours `list_changed` and an incompatible change to the shim or protocol, the same upgrade is classified as SOFT by lines 15/18 and HARD by line 21, so an implementation cannot select a tier deterministically.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/mcp-soft-upgrade.md:15

chunk_findings.detail: The accepted D-requirements-model decision in the intent says `MUST` has override options `waive|none`, but this line records `override = waive only`. A `strength=MUST` requirement with `override=none` would not be representable under this documented model, so the file misstates the operator decision and could drive the implementation to reject a valid accepted option.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/decisions/requirements.md:10

chunk_findings.detail: The operator decision says the always-on charter is capped at `[requirements].charter_tokens`, but the same section says the charter is “never trimmed” and that “over the cap is a doctor finding instead.” If an org sets `charter_tokens=100` and has enough MUSTs to require a 200-token charter, the configured cap is exceeded and only a doctor finding is produced; the knob no longer caps the charter as decided.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/decisions/requirements.md:24,29

chunk_findings.detail: The document records fixed rules and thresholds—the five-rung soft/hard classification, “one re-fetch within 10 s”, “two silent notifications in different sessions”, and the rejected transport options—without any file/CLI/MCP/prompt knob to change them. This violates [D-company-workflows] (warn): nothing ddflow ships is a fixed policy, and every rule/default/threshold must be changeable by users or company policies; for example, a team that needs a 30-second refetch window or must require a unix socket transport cannot override the shipped decision.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/mcp-soft-upgrade.md:13-26
